title: Трансмиссивные и региональные инфекции
terminology: Семейство является versioned regional disease matrix, а не тремя расплывчатыми карточками.
Каждая presentation имеет собственный pathogen/evidence route; варианты группируют болезни только по первичному решению и оборудованию.
Disease prior требует compatible geography, season, travel/import, vector or non-vector exposure and species.
Regional dataset updates меняют только будущие вероятности и не регенерируют сохранённого пациента.
Seropositivity обычно доказывает exposure/immune response, а не current causal disease.
Early acute disease can be seronegative; antibodies can persist in chronic/recovered states.
PCR/smear can be negative with low organism burden or after treatment; one negative smear never universally excludes infection.
Morula cell type and visual parasite morphology have limits and do not always identify species.
Coinfection is a valid state and must remain available when signs are severe or discordant.
Canine and feline heartworm testing algorithms differ because feline worm burden and antigen detectability are lower.
Microscopy remains available but is not omniscient; species-specific PCR/serology, paired titers and imaging have separate turnaround and cost.
The system does not generate antiparasitic/antimicrobial, transfusion, fluid, prevention, public-health protocol, drug or dose.

commonHistoryQuestions.prompt: Каковы lifetime/current geography, travel/import и точные даты?
Каковы season, vector sightings/removal и attachment context?
Были ли transfusion, fights, splenectomy или non-vector exposure?
Каков onset fever, lameness, bleeding, collapse и weight change?
Каковы raw CBC, reticulocytes, smear, platelets и organ values?
Есть ли coinfection, retrovirus или immune-mediated mimics?
Каковы cardiopulmonary, microfilaria, antigen, antibody и imaging data?
Какая region dataset version создала prior и сохранённый case?

variants.title: Бактериальные клещевые инфекции: Ehrlichia, Anaplasma и Borrelia
variants.diagnosticTruth: Compatible geography and vector exposure establish prior, while syndrome, serial CBC/organ injury and organism-specific PCR/serology timing distinguish active ehrlichiosis or anaplasmosis, Borrelia exposure from compatible clinical disease, and discordant acute, chronic or coinfected states.

presentations.complaint: A dog with compatible regional tick exposure has fever, lethargy, cytopenias, bleeding or shifting lameness.

historyAnswers.lifetime_current_geography_travel_import: Compatible location and dates are persisted.
historyAnswers.season_vector_sighting_removal_and_attac: Tick exposure is dated but is not diagnostic proof.
historyAnswers.onset_fever_lameness_bleeding_collapse_a: Syndrome and severity course are fixed.
historyAnswers.raw_cbc_reticulocytes_smear_platelets_an: Serial cytopenias and organ values remain raw.

examFindings.finding: Fever, cytopenia or morulae narrow the route but do not alone name the causal organism.

investigations.result: Compatible exposure prior established.
Cytopenia and organ severity staged.
Organism evidence interpreted by sample time.

followUp.timing: serial clinical, CBC, organ and organism-evidence review

outcomes.safe: The player stages severity and verifies organism evidence without turning exposure into diagnosis.
outcomes.unsafe: A tick, antibody or morula is treated as complete causal proof.

ownerCommunication: Explain that tick exposure raises suspicion, but active infection and its severity require compatible findings and correctly timed organism testing.

presentations.complaint: A Borrelia exposure test is positive in a dog with no signs, intermittent lameness, fever or possible renal involvement.

historyAnswers.lifetime_current_geography_travel_import: Endemic exposure and dates are explicit.
historyAnswers.onset_fever_lameness_bleeding_collapse_a: Clinical syndrome is present, absent or discordant by authored truth.
historyAnswers.raw_cbc_reticulocytes_smear_platelets_an: Urine and renal values are preserved without summary loss.

examFindings.finding: Seropositivity alone does not prove that Borrelia causes the current complaint.

investigations.result: Exposure prior documented.
Exposure is separated from compatible clinical disease.
Renal and systemic complications assessed.

followUp.timing: clinical and renal trend matched to the same exposure-test definition

outcomes.safe: Exposure-positive healthy, compatible clinical and renal-risk states remain distinct.
outcomes.unsafe: Every positive exposure test becomes active Lyme disease.

ownerCommunication: Explain that a positive exposure test is important context, but many exposed dogs are not clinically ill and kidney findings change urgency.

presentations.complaint: A compatible tick-exposed dog has discordant PCR, smear or serology, persistent antibody, or a severity pattern suggesting coinfection.

historyAnswers.organism_test_sample_time_titer_pcr_and_: Every result retains organism, method, sample and time.
historyAnswers.coinfection_retrovirus_and_immune_mediat: Coinfection and mimics remain open hypotheses.
historyAnswers.prevention_product_date_adherence_and_ga: Prevention history modifies prior but never erases disease.

examFindings.finding: Acute seronegativity, persistent antibody and low organism burden are expected states rather than data errors.

investigations.result: Discordance is interpreted against disease timing.
Exposure and compatible syndrome reviewed separately.
Same-case test definitions and response are retained.

followUp.timing: paired or serial evidence at clinically justified intervals

outcomes.safe: Discordance is preserved and resolved through timing, phenotype and serial evidence.
outcomes.unsafe: One negative or persistent antibody overwrites the authored infection state.

ownerCommunication: Explain why early and chronic tests can disagree and why additional timed evidence may be safer than an immediate binary label.

variants.title: Гемопаразитарные инфекции: Babesia и гемотропные микоплазмы
variants.diagnosticTruth: Hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and regenerative anemia require species-appropriate exposure, raw hematology and organ severity plus smear/PCR context; acute high-burden, chronic low-parasitemia, coinfected and feline carrier states remain distinct.

presentations.complaint: A dog after compatible tick, travel, fight or transfusion exposure has acute pallor, jaundice, dark urine, thrombocytopenia, weakness or collapse.

historyAnswers.transfusion_fight_splenectomy_and_nonvec: Vector and non-vector routes are dated.
historyAnswers.anemia_jaundice_urine_respiration_skin_e: Hemolysis and organ signs are explicit.
historyAnswers.raw_cbc_reticulocytes_smear_platelets_an: CBC, reticulocytes, smear and organ values remain raw.
historyAnswers.coinfection_retrovirus_and_immune_mediat: Coinfection and immune-mediated mimics are retained.

examFindings.finding: Hemolysis and collapse are treated before species certainty, without generated treatment instructions.

investigations.result: Immediate severity and transfer safety established.
Hemolysis, platelets and organ injury staged.
Babesia/species and coinfection route assessed.

followUp.timing: continuous emergency trend then serial hematology, organ and organism review

outcomes.safe: Emergency safety and hemolysis severity precede final species labeling.
outcomes.unsafe: A smear image triggers a generated drug or transfusion protocol.

ownerCommunication: Explain the immediate risk from anemia, bleeding and organ injury, the limits of a single smear, and the need for species/coinfection confirmation.

presentations.complaint: A dog has chronic or relapsing anemia/thrombocytopenia, a negative or equivocal smear, prior travel/fight/transfusion, or discordant coinfection evidence.

historyAnswers.organism_test_sample_time_titer_pcr_and_: Smear/PCR timing and pretest treatment are explicit.
historyAnswers.coinfection_retrovirus_and_immune_mediat: Coinfection and immune-mediated alternatives remain visible.

examFindings.finding: One negative smear cannot exclude low-burden or previously treated infection.

investigations.result: Low-burden/species route retained.
Chronic anemia and thrombocytopenia course measured.
Relapse and prevention history linked to the same case.

followUp.timing: serial hematology and same-method organism review

outcomes.safe: Low-burden, chronic, relapsing and coinfected states remain possible.
outcomes.unsafe: Negative microscopy closes the case or a new test silently changes prior truth.

ownerCommunication: Explain that organism numbers can be low and that travel, treatment and coinfection can make microscopy and molecular results disagree.

presentations.complaint: A cat has regenerative anemia, fever, pallor or jaundice, or a positive hemoplasma result without compatible illness.

historyAnswers.transfusion_fight_splenectomy_and_nonvec: Transfusion and splenic status are explicit.
historyAnswers.coinfection_retrovirus_and_immune_mediat: FeLV/FIV and immune-mediated/comorbid alternatives are retained.
historyAnswers.anemia_jaundice_urine_respiration_skin_e: Anemia severity and clinical compatibility are authored.

examFindings.finding: Smear sensitivity and morphology are limited, and PCR positivity can persist without being the sole cause of illness.

investigations.result: Regenerative anemia and severity assessed.
PCR, smear limits and carrier/comorbidity state interpreted.
Emergency safety route established.

followUp.timing: serial anemia, organism and comorbidity review

outcomes.safe: Clinical anemia and carrier/coinfection states are separated.
outcomes.unsafe: A smear-negative cat is cleared or every PCR-positive carrier is labeled actively ill.

ownerCommunication: Explain that the organism test must be interpreted with anemia severity and other feline infections, and that carrier states can complicate a binary answer.

variants.title: Региональные инфекции: лейшманиоз и дирофиляриоз собак и кошек
variants.diagnosticTruth: Versioned region, travel/import and prevention context gate generation; canine leishmaniosis and canine or feline heartworm require distinct species-specific clinical, laboratory, serologic, molecular and imaging evidence, with subclinical and discordant states preserved.

presentations.complaint: An imported or travelled dog has cutaneous, ocular, systemic or renal signs, or positive Leishmania evidence without clinical disease.

historyAnswers.lifetime_current_geography_travel_import: Endemic residence/travel/import and dates are persisted with dataset version.
historyAnswers.anemia_jaundice_urine_respiration_skin_e: Cutaneous, ocular, systemic and renal phenotype is authored.
historyAnswers.organism_test_sample_time_titer_pcr_and_: Quantitative serology and tissue/sample identity remain exact.
historyAnswers.regional_dataset_version_and_saved_case_: The saved case retains its original regional prior version.

examFindings.finding: Exposure or infection is not automatically clinical leishmaniosis.

investigations.result: Versioned region/travel prior established.
Serology and tissue/sample evidence interpreted together.
Systemic and renal involvement staged.

followUp.timing: serial clinical, renal and same-method organism-evidence review

outcomes.safe: Subclinical infection, clinical disease and renal severity remain separate authored states.
outcomes.unsafe: Travel or a positive result alone becomes disease, or treatment response becomes the diagnostic test.

ownerCommunication: Explain that regional exposure and infection do not always mean current illness, while kidney involvement changes urgency and long-term monitoring.

presentations.complaint: A dog from or travelling through a heartworm-risk region has positive, negative or discordant antigen/microfilaria tests with or without cardiopulmonary signs.

historyAnswers.lifetime_current_geography_travel_import: Exposure geography and maturation window are explicit.
historyAnswers.prevention_product_date_adherence_and_ga: Product dates and adherence gaps are retained without generating a regimen.
historyAnswers.cardiopulmonary_microfilaria_antigen_ant: Antigen, microfilaria, imaging and symptom data remain distinct.
historyAnswers.regional_dataset_version_and_saved_case_: Prior version remains attached to the generated patient.

examFindings.finding: A single test does not replace confirmation, maturation-window context or severity staging.

investigations.result: Exposure and prevention timeline fixed.
Canine antigen/microfilaria confirmation and imaging route applied.
Cardiopulmonary emergency and referral safety assessed.

followUp.timing: species-appropriate serial testing and cardiopulmonary reassessment

outcomes.safe: Canine infection evidence, discordance and cardiopulmonary stage remain linked but distinct.
outcomes.unsafe: One antigen result creates a treatment/prevention protocol or ignores severe cardiopulmonary signs.

ownerCommunication: Explain why antigen and microfilaria testing can disagree, why exposure timing matters, and why heart/lung staging determines urgency.

presentations.complaint: A cat from a heartworm-risk region has cough, dyspnea, vomiting, collapse or sudden death risk with negative or discordant antibody/antigen tests and low worm burden.

historyAnswers.lifetime_current_geography_travel_import: Exposure region and dates are explicit.
historyAnswers.prevention_product_date_adherence_and_ga: Prevention history changes prior, not truth.
historyAnswers.cardiopulmonary_microfilaria_antigen_ant: Feline antibody, antigen handling and imaging are separately recorded.
historyAnswers.anemia_jaundice_urine_respiration_skin_e: Respiratory/GI/collapse phenotype and severity are fixed.

examFindings.finding: Low female-worm burden can make antigen negative; antibody supports exposure but not necessarily current adult infection.

investigations.result: Feline exposure prior established.
Antibody, antigen limitations and imaging interpreted together.
Respiratory safety and referral route established.

followUp.timing: feline-specific serial clinical, serologic and imaging reassessment

outcomes.safe: Low-burden uncertainty and feline-specific evidence are preserved.
outcomes.unsafe: The canine antigen/microfilaria algorithm is copied to cats or one negative test excludes disease.

ownerCommunication: Explain that cats often carry very few worms, so no single blood test reliably answers every case and breathing difficulty requires urgent handling.

familyValidationRules: Reject if disease appears without compatible region/travel/exposure or species.
Reject if one tick sighting or positive antibody proves active disease, or negative early serology/one smear excludes infection.
Reject if all morulae/parasites are visually identified without limits or coinfection is impossible.
Reject if dog and cat heartworm testing is identical.
Reject if a saved case changes when regional prevalence data updates.
Reject if external results are instant.
Reject if code generates antiparasitic/antimicrobial, transfusion, fluid, prevention, public-health protocol or dose.
